newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy pledges continued help in rebuilding Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Italy pledges continued help in rebuilding Lebanon.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi told his Lebanese counterpart on Monday that Italy remained committed to the reconstruction of Lebanon, a government statement said.
Prodi told visiting Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri that Italy, which is Lebanon's biggest trading partner, confirmed its "interest in participating in the reconstruction of Lebanon".

Italy is one of the biggest financial contributors to the rebuilding effort after the devastating 1975-90 civil war. Major Italian companies are involved, particularly in rehabilitating the electricity network.
The statement said the two men discussed Middle East and Mediterranean issues and expressed the desire for "a renewed impulse (in bilateral relations) both on the political and economic fronts".
Al-Hariri, who earlier had an audience with Pope John Paul and met President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, invited Prodi to visit Lebanon soon. The invitation was accepted.
The Vatican announced earlier that the Pope would make a long-awaited trip to Lebanon on May 10-11.
